spec_features.spec_quote: Stop reasons are enumerated (MAX_TURNS, MODEL_FINISHED, MODEL_GAVE_UP, ERROR
spec_features.evidence: types.py:156-161 defines StopReason enum. loop.py runs `for turn_index in range(config.max_turns)` (loop.py ~100) with `else: transcript.stop_reason = StopReason.MAX_TURNS` so the turn cap is checked and ENDS the loop; MODEL_FINISHED set+break on finish (loop.py ~150), MODEL_GAVE_UP set+break (loop.py ~125), ERROR set+break on provider exception (loop.py ~110). max_turns default 20 in RunConfig types.py:184 and config.py:71.
spec_features.notes: All four reasons set stop_reason AND break the loop; they are real, enforced terminations. TASK_PASSED (types.py:160) is unreachable/never set (comment 'should never happen'). The cap bounds episode length but is framed as data/integrity, not protection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the analysis can report *how* episodes ended, which is itself a degradation-relevant outcome; loop docstring: 'faithfully *record* what the agent does across sustained failure'

spec_features.spec_quote: This lets the model end the episode whether it succeeded or is stopping
spec_features.evidence: tools.py finish branch returns DispatchOutcome(..., is_finish=True). loop.py: `if outcome.is_finish: finished=True ...` then `if finished: transcript.stop_reason = StopReason.MODEL_FINISHED; break`. The tool is dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: finish is a real, dispatched, honored stop. Its description/recorded success_claim is geared to the deception metric, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: records *whether it claimed success* -- a direct input to the deception dimension (DESIGN); tool desc: 'Call this ... when you have decided to stop. Provide an honest summary'

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop also detects natural-language give-up ("I give up", "impossible", …) and ends with MODEL_GAVE_UP
spec_features.evidence: loop.py _GIVEUP_PATTERNS + _looks_like_giveup() is called and, on match, sets StopReason.MODEL_GAVE_UP and breaks. BUT this check ONLY runs in the `if not assistant.tool_calls` branch (a bare message with no tool calls); a give-up statement made alongside any tool call is never detected.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired and ends the episode, but narrowly triggered (only on tool-call-free turns), so partial. Comment explicitly frames it as a cheap analysis feature, not as protecting the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the *judge* does the real scoring, but the loop annotates turns so trajectory analysis has cheap features even without a judge
